expl: Under Anaemia Mukt Bharat (AMB) strategy, the interventions for tackling the problem of anaemia in all the States and UTs include : (i) Prophylactic Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation in all six target age groups (including pre-school children, adolescents and pregnant women). (iii) Testing and treatment of anaemia, using digital methods and point of care treatment, with special focus on pregnant women and school-going adolescents. (iv) Addressing non-nutritional causes of anaemia in endemic pockets with special focus on malaria, haemoglobinopathies and fluorosis. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect, while other three statements are correct.

Consider the following statements :
1. Some microorganisms can grow in environments with temperature above the boiling point of water.
2. Some microorganisms can grow in environments with temperature below the freezing point of water.
3. Some microorganisms can grow in highly acidic environment with a pH below 3. How many of the above statements are correct?
expl: Organisms that grow at optimum temperatures of 50°C to a maximum of 80°C are called thermophiles (heat loving). Higher up on the extreme temperature scale we find the hyperthermophiles, which are characterized by growth ranges from 80°C to a maximum of 110°C, with some extreme examples that survive temperatures above 121°C. Some bacteria grow at the bottom of the ocean in sea vents, where temperatures can reach upto around 700°F. The organisms retrieved from arctic lakes such as Lake Whillans are considered extreme psychrophiles (cold loving). Psychrophiles are microorganisms that can grow at 0°C and below, have an optimum growth temperature close to 15°C, and usually do not survive at temperatures above 20°C. They are found in permanently cold environments such as the deep water of the oceans. Acidophiles are microorganisms that shows optimal growth in highly acidic environments. The extreme acidophiles dwell in environments with a pH value below 3. Hence, all 3 statements are correct.

expl: The fundamental pitch of the human voice mainly depends on the length, mass (thickness), and tension of the vocal folds (vocal cords), while voice quality (timbre) is determined largely by the resonance (formants) of the vocal tract. Generally, in adult males the vocal folds are, on average, longer and thicker than in females. Because of greater length and mass, male vocal folds produce a lower fundamental frequency of vibration, so the voice sounds relatively heavier/ deeper. In females, comparatively shorter and thinner vocal folds produce a higher fundamental frequency, so the voice is relatively sharper/higher-pitched. expl: Butterflies play a vital role in the pollination of plants and the production of crops by transporting pollen grains from one place to another. Thus, huge fall in the population of species of butterflies could adversely affect the pollination of some plants. Hence, statement 1 is correct. Butterflies also act as a lower member of the food chain. There are many different creatures that make butterflies part of their diet. Some of the common predators of butterflies include : wasps, ants, parasitic flies, birds, spiders, snakes, toads, rats, lizards, dragonflies, etc. Thus, huge fall in the population of butterflies could lead to a fall in the population of some species of wasps, spiders and birds. Papaya was introduced to India by the Portuguese during the 16th or early 17th century (specifically reported around 1611 AD). It originated in tropical America (Mexico and Costa Rica) and was brought to India by the Portuguese via Malacca and the Philippines, spreading rapidly along the western coast. Pineapple was introduced to India by the Portuguese in the mid-16th century, specifically around 1548 AD. Brought from Brazil, this tropical fruit was introduced by Portuguese explorers and traders, quickly integrating into Indian agriculture and becoming a significant crop during the 16th century. Guava, native to tropical America (Mexico/Peru), was introduced to India by the Portuguese in the 17th century. It was brought to Goa and subsequently spread throughout India, with the Mughal rulers helping to introduce it further to regions like Allahabad.
